children: shares closed lower for the third straight session on Wednesday after Deutsche Bank downgraded the Swiss drugmaker, citing recent failures in a pair of its late-stage trials that sent the stock sharply lower in the prior session.

The Basel, Switzerland-based company lost more than 13% on Tuesday after its RNA-based therapy del-desiran, added from its $12B buyout of Avidity Bio in 2025, failed in a Phase 3 trial for a rare muscle-wasting disease called
The setback piled pressure on a company reeling from its Friday announcement of another late-stage trial failure for a heart disease therapy it developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals

“Without further details, we do not know to what extent this raises concerns over the broader Avidity antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates platform,” analyst Emmanuel Papadakis wrote as he downgraded Novartis

Acknowledging that the setback “continues a run of very challenging deal return metrics” for the company, Papadakis wrote that “it has now become a lot harder to argue for significant upside” in a stock currently trading at 14x FY27 after the selloff. The analyst cut his price target on NVS to CHF120 from CHF140.

title: Novartis extends selloff as Deutsche Bank cuts on twin drug trial setbacks
